newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Top Colombian law man dismissed from office.
newsitem.headline: Top Colombian law man dismissed from office.

text.p: Colombia's Supreme Court has ordered the dismissal of Attorney General Orlando Vasquez Velasquez, five months after he was arrested on drug corruption charges, judicial sources said on Friday.

They said the court voted late Thursday by an overwhelming 22-1 majority to remove the country's top law officer, citing a catalogue of charges against him including obstruction of justice and abuse of power.

The court was to notify the Senate of its unprecedented ruling on Friday, they added. Approval of the order is a formality because it is not subject to appeal and must be strictly complied with by the legislative branch.

In brief remarks to reporters early Friday before departing on an official visit to Asia, President Ernesto Samper said that while the Supreme Court's decision was binding, he trusted that Vasquez would have an opportunity to defend himself in public.
He said he would name a possible replacement for Vasquez when the Senate asked him to do so.

Vasquez, a former interior minister and ruling Liberal Party senator, was released in August from police detention in the capital, where he had been held since early May on charges that he accepted thousands of dollars in payments from leading drug traffickers, both before and after he was sworn in as attorney general in 1994.
Vasquez has denied any wrongdoing. His U.S. travel visa was revoked in April because of his alleged links to drug lords.

Guillermo Pallomari, the self-confessed Cali drug cartel treasurer who surrendered to U.S. drug agents in the United States last year, has testified that Vasquez had closer ties with the cartel's jailed leaders than perhaps any other politician in Colombia.
Vasquez was suspended from office by the Supreme Court shortly before his arrest in May but continued to hold the title of attorney general.
